# Common Usage

## Lists

Unnumbered lists are generated automatically in Quarto by starting a line with `-` or `*` or `+`.

- So a list can start like this,
- Then continues
     + And a sublist can start after that
          * And even more.
          
1. Numbered lists are the same
     i. And subnumbered lists
          a. And more.
          
## Tables

Tables are separated using `|` with alignments `:--:`.

| Right | Left | Default | Centre |
|------:|:-----|---------|:------:|
|   12  |  12  |    12   |    12  |
|  123  |  123 |   123   |   123  |
|    1  |    1 |     1   |     1  |

Some more sophisticated tables can be done with merged cells:

+------+-----------+---------------------------------------------------+
| Week | Day       | Topic                                             |
+======+===========+===================================================+
| 1    | Tuesday   | - Chapter 1                                       |
+      +-----------+---------------------------------------------------+
|      | Thursday  | - Chapter 2                                       |
|      |           | - Section 2.1                                     |
|      |           | - Section 2.2                                     |
+      +-----------+---------------------------------------------------+
|      | Friday    | - Chapter 3                                       |
+------+-----------+---------------------------------------------------+
| 2    | Monday    | - Section 3.1.1a                                  |
|      |           | - Section 3.1.5                                   |
+      +-----------+---------------------------------------------------+
|      | Wednesday | - Chapter 4                                       |
|      |           | - Chapter 5                                       |
+------+-----------+---------------------------------------------------+

## Blocks

### Callout Blocks

Callout blocks can be very useful for separating information.  Generally, the callout blocks start with `:::{.callout-TYPE}` and ends with `:::`.  Each callout block style has its own reserved syntax.

:::{.callout-note}
Note nte
:::

:::{.callout-warning}
Warning wrn
:::

:::{.callout-important}
Important imp
:::

:::{.callout-tip}
Tip tip
:::

:::{.callout-caution}
Caution cau
:::

#### Options

Callout blocks can also have their icons removed with `icon=false` and be collapsible using `collapse=true`.  By default, the callout box will be collapsible and with an icon.

:::{.callout-caution collapse=true icon=false}
Collapsible caution with no icon
:::

Callout boxes can also be titles with `##` as the first line of the callout box itself.  They can also be labelled with `#TYPE-Label` and referenced with `@TYPE-Label`.

:::{#nte-BoxLabel .callout-note}
## Note Box With Title and Reference

Note with stuff
:::

Note box with label @nte-BoxLabel.

### Quotes

If there is a specific quote, then `Blockquote` needs to be used.

> Blockquote

### Footnotes

Footnotes can also be placed in Quarto using `[^LABEL]` and the footnote will hover over the clicker[^FN].

[^FN]: Like this.

## Theorems etc.

Theorems, Definitions and such have their own environment.  Generally, the callout blocks start with `:::{.callout-TYPE}` and ends with `:::`, each one has its own reserved syntax.

:::{#def-SomeDef}
## Definition
def
:::

:::{#thm-SomeThm}
## Theorem
thm
:::

:::{#cor-SomeCor}
## Corollary
cor
:::

:::{#lem-SomeLem}
## Lemma
lem
:::

:::{#prp-SomeProp}
## Proposition
prp
:::

:::{#cnj-SomeConj}
## Conjecture
cnj
:::

:::{#exm-SomeEg}
## Example
exm
:::

:::{#exr-SomeEx}
## Excersise
exr
:::

:::{#sol-SomeSol}
## Solution
sol
:::

:::{#rem-SomeRem}
## Remark
rem
:::

This can be referenced as @thm-SomeThm.

## Output Specific Formats

Sometimes there are some outputs that will be displayed only for one format only and not others (this is useful when there are moving images or embedded dynamic changes).  This can be used using a code block as `:::{.content-visible when-format="TYPE"` where `TYPE` is `html`, `pdf` or `docx`.

:::{.content-visible when-format="html"}
Things that only appear in HTML version.
:::

:::{.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
Things that only appear in PDF version.
:::

:::{.content-visible when-format="docx"}
Things that only appear in docx version.
:::

## Figures

Figures can be inserted using `![Image caption.](figure/directory.png){width=100% fig-align="center" fig-alt="Alternative caption." #fig-FIGURE_LABEL}`.  All images are clickable and on a lightbox.

![Image caption here.  The image is clickable to enlarge.](figures/image.png){width=100% fig-align="center" fig-alt="Alternative caption" #fig-Figure}

Figure can be referenced using `@fig-FIGURE_LABEL` to give @fig-Figure.

## Codes

Some codes can be displayed or executed directly in Quarto.  Not every programming language can be executed but Python is one that can be.  Executable Python code blocks require `{python}` but non executable one start with `python`.  Code blocks can also be labelled and captioned with `lst-label` and `lst-cap`.

```{python}
#| lst-label: lst-Sample
#| lst-cap:  Sample caption for code.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

S = 0

for n in range(1,10):
    S = S+n
    plt.plot(n,S,'.k',ms=10)

print(S)
```

Codes can be referenced using `@lst-Sample`, like @lst-Sample.

## Writing Mathematics

In Quarto, maths can be written exactly as it is written in LaTeX in terms of syntax.  Maths can be written in-line using `$...$` as $x=1$, or can be written separately using `$$...$$` as
$$
x=1.
$$

Equations can also be labelled using `#eq-NAME` as
$$
x=\frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}
$${#eq-Equation}
and can be referenced using `@` as @eq-Equation.

Many maths shortcuts have been built into the `_macros.qmd` file.
